terms.comment: The council of the elders, named from senex, as Cicero says (Sen. 19). The Roman senate was a standing council of former magistrates, enrolled by the censors and sitting for life; it advised the magistrates, and its decrees (senātūs cōnsulta) were not laws. A modern senate is the upper house of a parliament and votes on laws; Latin keeps the word for it (Levi–Bini p. 46, of the Italian Senate). The senate house is cūria (Traupman 180).

terms.comment: Tursellinus’s name (1652) for the House of Lords; camera, classically a vaulted room (Lewis & Short), is Morgan–Owens’s word for a chamber of a parliament.
senātūs cōnsultum facere, to pass a decree of the senate.
